algorithm.id: legacy_child_id(root, path) = md5('taskfold.child-row.v1|' || lower(root) || '|' || path joined by U+001F) formatted 8-4-4-4-12 (no version bits).
algorithm.path_segment: SubtaskTree.childKey: the node id when it is a non-empty string, else '@index'. When several siblings share a key, each of them uses '@index' instead.
algorithm.levels: A child of the root is level 1. A node deeper than level 10 is re-parented to its level-9 ancestor (the deepest the server's ten-ancestor guard allows is level 10). Its id still comes from its real path. child_order is index+1 among the original siblings; re-parented nodes get 1000 + their running count in pre-order. Nodes deeper than level 32 are skipped (depth_over_32).
algorithm.skip_reasons: not_an_object, missing_title (object without a string title), empty_title (blank), depth_over_32, id_collision. A skipped node takes its whole branch with it; descendants counts the nodes lost.
algorithm.field_mapping: title, description, completed, completed_at, priority, due_date, due_time, time_zone, scheduled_at, deadline_date, duration_minutes, labels, comments, attachments, reminder_specs, is_heading, created_at, assigned_to copy when their JSON type is right; anything else (or a mistyped known key) goes to source_metadata.taskfold_legacy_child. assigned_to survives only when the root has a project. user_id, project_id, section_id come from the root.
